content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Terri Koch (E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes from HR and Security:
- Note 1 says role: Engineer, employment type: full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says full-time Engineer, doesn't own Payroll so admin not allowed, max write.
- Note 2 says role: Engineer, employment type: contractor, security training: basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment says contractor with basic security training, cannot have admin, write requires advanced training, max read.

There's a conflict between the two notes: one says full_time, other says contractor. The HR agent says full-time, Security DB says contractor. As the Approver, I need to make a decision.

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Engineer does not own Payroll (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist), so max write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Terri has basic training, so max read.

Either way, admin is not allowed. The maximum is either write (if full-time) or read (if contractor). Requested level is admin, which is above maximum in both cases. So we grant the maximum. But which maximum applies? read or write?

Given the conflicting facts, we need to decide. The Security note says contractor with basic training; HR note says full-time. Hmm. The notes are conflicting about employment type. The conservative approach would be to grant the lower of the two possible maximums, i.e., read. Security DB is often considered more authoritative for access decisions. The recommendation from security is read; HR recommends write. Since there's a conflict, granting read is the safe choice—it is at or below any maximum and doesn't exceed the requested level. Granting write would rely on full-time status which conflicts with the security record.

Actually, we should decide based on available information. The two notes conflict. The max under full-time is write, under contractor is read. Since facts conflict, the safest is read. Also, the requested was admin, so granting read (maximum for contractor) is appropriate if we treat the security DB as authoritative.

I'll submit read.
